subject: Veridian Dedicated: GPU SKU tradeoffs & reserve sizing
body:
From: Samir Rao <samir@veridian.ai>

Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: initial constraints and goals

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A quick follow-up from our side as we sketch the commercial ask:

- Target: production rollout in Q4, ~1M monthly gen tokens initially, ramp to 5M over 6 months.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 400ms for typical user flows (prompt 1.5k tokens, response ~150 tokens).
- Workload: mixture of short chat + batched batch-embed queries; 30% long-context workflows (>=8k context).
- Data residency: US only.

We know you discussed H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs in the deck; can you recommend a reserve sizing and SKU hedge that balances memory headroom for long-context vs token-cost efficiency for high-throughput chat? Also, any rough guidance on pricing delta between H100 reserve vs L4-heavy hybrid?

If helpful, I can loop in our procurement team next week.

Samir
CTO, Veridian AI

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@veridian.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity: initial constraints and goals

Samir — thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a practical sizing cadence that balances headroom and cost while keeping options for burst. I kept the math conservative to avoid OOMs on long-context requests.

Summary recommendation (first 3 months):
- Reserve: 8 H100 GPUs (80 GB) allocated to long-context model variants to satisfy the 30% long-context traffic. This provides KV cache headroom and avoids offloading for 8k+ sequences.
- Reserve: 6 L4 GPUs (48 GB equiv per instance via multi-instance) for short chat and embedding workloads; cheaper per-token and good for high concurrency.
- Burst pool: allow 20% burst into on-demand A100 slots for peak events (30–60 minute windows) with auto-fallback to smaller shipments if headroom is exceeded.

Rationale and tradeoffs:
- H100: best-in-class memory bandwidth and large model memory allow single-GPU serving of many of today's long-context model variants without tiling. That simplifies KV management and keeps 95p latency tight. Cost: highest per-hour but value for long-context.
- A100: solid middle ground for many transformer sizes; lower memory than H100 for large context, but good throughput for medium-length prompts. Useful as a burst/backfill option if reserve H100s are exhausted.
- L4: great for short-turn chats and embeddings; much lower cost per token. Limited for >8k contexts unless you shard/tiling aggressively (which increases latency variance).

Operational notes (how we'd implement):
1) Route policy: prefix long-context requests to H100 pool; short-chat to L4 pool. Use latency SLO rules to re-route to A100 burst when H100 latency climbs.
2) Cache strategy: enable prefix KV caching on H100s to reduce repeated token costs for multi-turn flows.
3) Autoscaling and warm-up: maintain one warm spare H100 in reserve to reduce cold start tail latency for sudden traffic pattern changes.
4) Quantization: keep long-context models in FP16/TF32 on H100; we can trial 4-bit quant on L4 for chat throughput.

Sizing math (back-of-envelope):
- Assumptions: avg generation 150 tokens, 1M monthly gen tokens ~ 30k gen calls/month; 95th latency target implies concurrency <= 80 sustained across peak windows.
- H100: approx 10–12 concurrent long-context sessions per GPU under our model profile => 8 H100 ~= 80–96 concurrent long-context capacity.
- L4: approx 100–150 concurrent short-chat sessions per GPU => 6 L4 ~= 600–900 concurrent short-chat capacity.

Price delta (ballpark):
- Reserve H100 seat-month ~ 6–8x the cost of an L4 seat-month (depending on commitment). A100 on-demand burst sits between them but closer to H100 in some markets. Exact numbers we’ll surface to procurement.

Attachments: I attached a simple worksheet with the calculator and a short latency benchmark PDF to illustrate concurrency numbers.

If that matches your expectation I’ll hand this to Lauren to surface formal pricing and an ops playbook for the SLA.

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: veridian-sku-sizing.xlsx, latency-benchmarks.pdf
